title: Roos triangle and Milnor exact sequence
statement:
For every $M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$, the tower category
being that of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], the transition maps
define an endomorphism $s$ of $R\!\prod_nM_n$, and the defining Roos triangle
of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is the functorial distinguished
triangle

$$
 \Rlim M_\bullet\longrightarrow R\!\prod_nM_n
 \xrightarrow{1-s}R\!\prod_nM_n
 \longrightarrow(\Rlim M_\bullet)[1].
$$

If $U$ is a weakly contractible quasi-compact object of $T_{\Proet}$, then
for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ this triangle induces the functorial exact sequence

$$
 0\to\varprojlim{}^1_nH^{i-1}(U,M_n)
 \to H^i(U,\Rlim M_\bullet)
 \to\varprojlim_nH^i(U,M_n)\to0.
$$

(*Source note:* the canonical triangle is Stacks Project, More on Algebra,
Lemma 15.88.9 (Tag [07KX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KX)): for
$K=(K_n^\bullet)$ in $D(\textit{Ab}(\mathbf N))$ there is a canonical
distinguished triangle $R\lim K\to\prod_nK_n^\bullet\to\prod_nK_n^\bullet\to
R\lim K[1]$, so that $R\lim K$ is a derived limit in the sense of Definition
13.34.1 (Tag [08TC](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08TC)); the
associated short exact sequences are Lemma 15.88.10 (Tag
[07KY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KY): the long exact cohomology
sequence breaks up into $0\to R^1\lim_nH^{p-1}(K_n^\bullet)\to H^p(R\lim
K)\to\lim_nH^p(K_n^\bullet)\to0$), and the representation of $\Rlim$ by the
two-term complex $\prod A_n\to\prod A_n$, $(x_n)\mapsto(x_n-f_{n+1}(x_{n+1}))$,
in degrees $0,1$, together with $R^p\lim A_n=0$ for $p>1$, is Lemma 15.88.1
(Tag [07KW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07KW)). The Stacks entries
are stated for towers of abelian groups; the blueprint states the same
triangle for the tower category $\operatorname{Tow}_A(T)$ over $T_{\Proet}$
with $A_T$-coefficients, where the two derived products are those of
[prop-weil-pbc-derived-product-representation], and it evaluates the Milnor
sequence at a weakly contractible quasi-compact $U\in T_{\Proet}$, which is
the form in which it is used below.)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)$ and represent $M_\bullet$ by an integer cochain complex $C$ of strict towers. Its evaluations $C_n$ are complexes with chain maps $t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$. Countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact and sectionwise by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] identifies the localization of the termwise product complex $P=\prod_n C_n$ with the product of the evaluations in $D(\mathcal A)$ and gives $H^j(P)=\prod_n H^j(C_n)$. Define $s:P\to P$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n s=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. The chain-map equation follows after every projection from $d t_n=t_n d$, and the projections are jointly faithful. Thus $d_P(1-s)=(1-s)d_P$.

source.place: Tag 07KC, label lemma-products; Tag 08TC, label definition-derived-limit

proof.text: Set $h=1-s$ and form the explicit complex $L(C)=\operatorname{Cone}(h)[-1]$, so that $L(C)^j=P^{j-1}\oplus P^j$ and $d(y,x)=(-d_Py-hx,d_Px)$. The maps $p:L(C)\to P$, $p(y,x)=x$, and $\delta:P\to L(C)[1]$, $\delta(y)=(y,0)$, give $L(C)\xrightarrow p P\xrightarrow h P\xrightarrow\delta L(C)[1]$. This is the inverse rotation of the mapping-cone triangle, with the cone/rotation signs in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-triangulated-category]; therefore it is distinguished. By [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] it is a Roos triangle for the evaluated tower. This constructs a model of the derived limit; it does not assert that the definition by a triangle has already chosen a functor.

For a map $u:C\to C'$ of strict tower complexes, the product map $v=\prod_nu_n$ satisfies $vh=h'v$ since $u_nt_n=t'_nu_{n+1}$. On $L(C)$ define $L(u)(y,x)=(vy,vx)$. It is a chain map because $d_{L(C^{\prime})}(vy,vx)=(-d_{P^{\prime}}vy-h^{\prime} vx,d_{P^{\prime}}vx)=(-v d_Py-vhx,v d_Px)=L(u)d_{L(C)}(y,x)$. Moreover $p^{\prime} L(u)(y,x)=vx=vp(y,x)$ and $L(u)[1]\delta(y)=(vy,0)=\delta^{\prime} v(y)$, while $vh=h^{\prime} v$ is the middle square. The diagonal map of an identity is the identity and the composite of two diagonal maps is the diagonal of their composite, so these maps define a functor and a natural triangle on strict tower complexes. If $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes, exact evaluation makes every $u_n$ a quasi-isomorphism, and [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] makes $Q(v)$ an isomorphism. In the resulting morphism of distinguished triangles the two product components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $Q(L(u))$ an isomorphism. The localization property of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] now factors the strict cone construction, its maps and its natural triangle through $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$. This proves the functorial assertion by a functorial realization of the derived-limit property. No functorial choice of cones for arbitrary maps in a triangulated category is used.

source.place: Tag 014F, label lemma-functorial-cone (strict square, zero homotopy); Tag 014A, label lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle; Tag 05RU, localization

proof.text: Fix the weakly contractible object $U$. Here weakly contractible means that every surjection of sheaves of sets induces a surjection on sections over $U$ (Sites Tag 090L, label definition-w-contractible). Evaluation on abelian sheaves is left exact, since kernels are sectionwise; it is right exact because weak contractibility makes any sheaf-surjection surjective on $U$-sections. This is exactly the two-line argument of Cohomology on Sites Tag 0946 (label lemma-w-contractible), not a vanishing claim for arbitrary objects of the site. The exact forgetful functor and sectionwise limits of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] therefore show that $E_U=\Gamma(U,-):\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is exact and preserves countable products. In particular this applies to the completed ring sheaf $A_T$, without requiring it to be a finite constant ring.

source.place: Tag 0946, label lemma-w-contractible (1), with Sites Tag 090L, label definition-w-contractible

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to the exact additive functor $E_U$. Its termwise application carries the constructed Roos triangle to a distinguished triangle in $D(\mathrm{Ab})$. It computes derived sections on this exact evaluation object: any resolution quasi-isomorphism remains a quasi-isomorphism after $E_U$, so $H^j(U,K)=H^j(E_U K)$, including unbounded $K$. Since $E_U$ preserves the termwise products and abelian groups have exact products by [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products], [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] applied to $\mathrm{Ab}$ identifies $H^j(E_UP)$ with $\prod_n H^j(U,M_n)$. By the equations for the projections defining $s$, the induced map is $h_j((a_n))=(a_n-(t_n)_*a_{n+1})$. The long exact sequence of [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] thus contains the exact segment $\prod_n H^{i-1}(U,M_n)\xrightarrow{h_{i-1}}\prod_n H^{i-1}(U,M_n)\xrightarrow{\partial}H^i(U,L(C))\xrightarrow b\prod_n H^i(U,M_n)\xrightarrow{h_i}\prod_n H^i(U,M_n)$.

source.place: Tag 07KY, label lemma-break-long-exact-sequence, proof (long exact sequence); derived.tex Tag 07KC, label lemma-products

proof.text: For the abelian-group towers $B_n^j=H^j(U,M_n)$, [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups] identifies $\ker h_j=\varprojlim_nB_n^j$ and $\operatorname{coker}h_j=R^1\varprojlim_nB_n^j$. Since $\partial\circ h_{i-1}=0$, factor $\partial$ through $\operatorname{coker}h_{i-1}$; exactness in the preceding segment makes the resulting map $\operatorname{coker}h_{i-1}\to H^i(U,L(C))$ injective with image $\ker b$. Since $\operatorname{im}b=\ker h_i$, corestricting $b$ to $\ker h_i$ is surjective. These are the required short exact sequence and its maps. This argument takes the kernel and cokernel in abelian groups after evaluation, and does not infer a sheaf statement from Tag 07KW without an exact-product hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 07KW, label lemma-compute-Rlim (1),(2); Tag 07KY, label lemma-break-long-exact-sequence, proof

proof.text: For a morphism of tower objects, step 3 gives a morphism of the functorially realized Roos triangles; evaluation carries it to a morphism of distinguished triangles. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] the long exact sequences commute also at the connecting maps, not only at the product maps. The kernel/cokernel identifications of [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups] are natural. Consequently the induced maps on the cokernel of $h_{i-1}$, the middle cohomology group, and the kernel of $h_i$ commute with the two maps of step 6. This proves functoriality of the displayed short exact sequence. For restriction along $V\to U$ between weakly contractible test objects, write $r_P:E_UP\to E_VP$ for the componentwise restriction chain map. Restrictions commute with the differentials and $t_n$, so $r_Ph_U=h_Vr_P$. Define $r_L(y,x)=(r_Py,r_Px)$; then $d_Vr_L=r_Ld_U$, $p_Vr_L=r_Pp_U$ and $r_L[1]\delta_U=\delta_Vr_P$ by the displayed formulas. These maps give a morphism of the evaluated distinguished triangles, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] yields $H^i(r_L)\partial_U=\partial_VH^{i-1}(r_P)$. Restricting the product map to $\ker h_i$ and passing to $\operatorname{coker}h_{i-1}$ therefore gives commuting squares for both arrows of the short exact sequence, proving compatibility with restriction.
